message.content:
Here’s a quick‑look table of the **long weekends** that occurred in Canada during 2023.  
(“Long weekend” means a holiday that falls on a weekday, giving you at least two consecutive days off.)

| Date(s) | Holiday | Notes |
|---------|---------|-------|
| **Jan 1–3** | New Year’s Day (Mon) | 1 day holiday + weekend |
| **Feb 20–22** | Family Day (Mon) – Alberta, Saskatchewan, Ontario | 1 day holiday + weekend |
| **Apr 7–9** | Good Friday (Fri) | 1 day holiday + weekend |
| **May 22–24** | Victoria Day (Mon) | 1 day holiday + weekend |
| **Jul 1–3** | Canada Day (Sat) | Holiday on Saturday; long weekend includes the following Monday |
| **Sep 4–6** | Labour Day (Mon) | 1 day holiday + weekend |
| **Oct 9–11** | Thanksgiving (Mon) | 1 day holiday + weekend |
| **Nov 11–13** | Remembrance Day (Mon) | 1 day holiday + weekend |
| **Dec 25–27** | Christmas Day (Mon) + Boxing Day (Tue) | Two holidays back‑to‑back; long weekend spans Mon–Wed |

> **Tip for your app:**  
> • If a holiday falls on a weekend, Canada typically observes it on the nearest weekday (e.g., if Canada Day were on Sunday, the holiday would be observed on Monday).  
> • Some provinces have additional holidays (e.g., St. Patrick’s Day in Newfoundland & Labrador) that can create extra long weekends—consider adding a flag to let users filter by province.

Feel free to copy this table into your holiday‑planning app or let me know if you’d like it formatted differently!
